title: Macbeth Analysis in Action
welcome_lead: Apply your knowledge to Lady Macbeth, the witches and the changing power balance through Acts 1-5.
meta_desc: GCSE English Literature — Macbeth character and theme analysis through Acts 1-5.
final_note: You traced Lady Macbeth's manipulation, the witches' equivocation and the inversion of natural order.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Lady Macbeth attacks her husband's masculinity: 'When you durst do it, then you were a man.'

She also invokes the supernatural: 'unsex me here, and fill me from the crown to the toe top-full of direst cruelty.' She wills herself out of her gender to commit regicide.

The witches deal in equivocation — truth that misleads.

'None of woman born shall harm Macbeth' is technically true (Macduff was 'untimely ripp'd' by C-section), but Macbeth hears it as immortality. Their language traps him.

After Duncan's murder, horses eat each other and an owl kills a falcon.

Jacobeans believed the king embodied natural order. Killing him fractures the cosmos — Shakespeare flatters his patron, James I, who survived an assassination attempt in 1605.

mcqs.q: What does Lady Macbeth ask the spirits to do in her famous soliloquy?
options: Crown her queen
Unsex her
Bring back her child
Kill Duncan themselves

mcqs.q: Why is Macduff able to kill Macbeth despite the prophecy?
options: He hides his identity
He was born by Caesarean section
He uses magic
He is in fact a woman

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
A theme is the title of the book.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a theme and a symbol?
options: A theme is an abstract idea or concern the text explores (e.g. mortality); a symbol is a concrete image that stands for something else (e.g. a skull).
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
A theme is the title of the book.
Themes are just symbols repeated through the book.
